## Published Concept Explainers (5)
- **Habitat fragmentation (生境破碎化)**: The landscape-scale process involving both habitat loss (reduction in total area H) and habitat fragmentation per se (breaking apart of habitat while controlling for H). / 景观中连续生境在面积减少的同时被分割为更小、更孤立的斑块；机制分析须区分生境丧失（总面积 H 减少）与控制 H 后的纯粹破碎化。
  - Chinese URL: https://juanli.me/seeing-ecology/habitat-fragmentation/zh/
  - English URL: https://juanli.me/seeing-ecology/habitat-fragmentation/en/
  - Primary Literature: Fahrig 2003, 2013, 2017 · Laurance et al. 2011 · Haddad et al. 2015 · Fletcher et al. 2018 · Damschen et al. 2019 · Gonçalves-Souza et al. 2025
- **Keystone species (关键种)**: A species whose impact on its community or ecosystem is large, and disproportionately large relative to its abundance. / 对群落或生态系统的影响很大，且相对于其丰度而言不成比例地大的物种。
  - Chinese URL: https://juanli.me/seeing-ecology/keystone/zh/
  - English URL: https://juanli.me/seeing-ecology/keystone/en/
  - Primary Literature: Paine 1966, 1969 · Power et al. 1996 · Estes et al. 2011
- **Umbrella species (伞护种)**: A candidate species whose conservation is expected to confer protection to co-occurring species; actual effectiveness requires both spatial null-model and management-benefit validation. / 预期通过保护它，也能保护许多同域自然共存物种的候选物种；具体伞护效果须经空间零模型与管理净益两层实证检验。
  - Chinese URL: https://juanli.me/seeing-ecology/umbrella/zh/
  - English URL: https://juanli.me/seeing-ecology/umbrella/en/
  - Primary Literature: Wilcox 1984 · Fleishman et al. 2000 · Roberge & Angelstam 2004 · Carlisle et al. 2018
- **Flagship species (旗舰种)**: A species selected as the focus of a conservation marketing campaign based on traits that appeal to a target audience, used to rally awareness, support, and funding. / 凭契合目标受众的特征被选作保护营销重心，用来凝聚关注、共识与资金支持的物种。
  - Chinese URL: https://juanli.me/seeing-ecology/flagship/zh/
  - English URL: https://juanli.me/seeing-ecology/flagship/en/
  - Primary Literature: Heywood 1995 · Walpole & Leader-Williams 2002 · Veríssimo et al. 2011
- **Biodiversity credits (生物多样性信用)**: A certificate representing a measured, evidence-based positive biodiversity outcome that is additional and durable. Frameworks differ on use; this note focuses on voluntary, non-offset credits for nature contributions. / 代表经测量、有证据支持、具有额外性与持久性的正向生物多样性成果的凭证。不同框架对其使用方式有不同规定；本页重点讨论用于自然贡献的非抵消型自愿信用。
  - Chinese URL: https://juanli.me/seeing-ecology/biodiversity-credits/zh/
  - English URL: https://juanli.me/seeing-ecology/biodiversity-credits/en/
  - Primary Literature: KMGBF 2022 · 彭昀月等 2024 · Wauchope et al. 2024 · Wunder et al. 2025 · 彭昀月, 彭奎等 2026

## Upcoming Concept Nodes in the Graph (4)
- **Indicator species (指示种)**: A species whose presence, abundance, or physiological state reflects environmental conditions, disturbance, or community richness. (Landres et al. 1988 · Caro & O'Doherty 1999)
- **Metapopulation & source–sink (集合种群与源-汇动态)**: Spatially discrete local populations linked by dispersal, encompassing both extinction–recolonization balance (Levins 1969; Hanski 1998) and source–sink dynamics where immigration sustains occupancy in sinks with negative local growth (Pulliam 1988). (Levins 1969 · Pulliam 1988 · Hanski 1998)
- **Trophic cascade (营养级联)**: Indirect top-down effects of predators transmitted across two or more trophic links via density or behavioral pathways; the net direction on primary producers alternates with chain length (releasing plants in 3-level chains, suppressing them in 4-level chains). (Paine 1980 · Carpenter et al. 1985 · Estes et al. 2011 · Ripple et al. 2016)
- **Ecological niche (生态位)**: The n-dimensional hypervolume of environmental conditions and resources permitting positive growth (fundamental niche) versus the subset occupied under biotic interactions and dispersal constraints (realized niche). (Grinnell 1917 · Elton 1927 · Hutchinson 1957 · Soberón 2007)
